artifacts.title: The human-attention tag
artifacts.summary: T decided, and this Decision seals, that every step in every roadmap artifact — Trajectory legs and Phase steps alike — is evaluated by one question: can an AI agent perform this step? If it can, the step carries nothing. If it is work an agent cannot do no matter what, the step carries the inline marker **[HUMAN ATTENTION]**, and absence of the marker is itself an assertion that the work is AI-performable. The work that qualifies is purchases and payments, identity and credentials and consent, physical acts and acts in T's own relationships, taste and appetite T has reserved, choices whose content is T's judgment, and anything requiring a human to be answerable. Rejected: tagging by 'needs approval' — this estate approves everything by law, so such a tag would mark every step and discriminate nothing; it is kept only as a guard against drift and is no part of the criterion — plus a frontmatter classifier (the unit classified is the step, and a classifier cannot address a step), a graded scale (invites argument where the useful question is binary), and marking the AI-doable inverse (the estate marks the exception, and the exception is the smaller set). Grey band rule: tag the step if any part of it is human-only and say in the step what the agent does up to that line — a tag is a boundary marker, not an abdication. Binds chart and phase outputs from 2026-08-28 forward, does not rewrite sealed roadmaps, does bind the unmerged idea-0004 roadmap; reopens if agent capability swallows a tagged category, if the tag stops discriminating by appearing nearly everywhere or nowhere, or if a tagged step is ever completed without T's hands. It governs the form of roadmaps and not their content, and it does not touch idea-0004's two still-owed decisions, which remain open. Amended in review on 2026-08-31 at T's instruction to lead with the plain capability question and demote the approval contrast to a rejected alternative; the rule itself is unchanged.

artifacts.title: The record is complete; the view of it is missing
artifacts.summary: The estate's record is complete but illegible at a glance — every fact a map needs is in frontmatter, yet the file tree renders storage rather than travel, and T, a visual learner, cannot see the thing that has been built. The framing takes the map before the tree (the lineage graph is derivable today; the hierarchy T's words name is not), takes read-only before dispatch (a surface that writes or steers collides with the writer seam and the unaddressable steering layer), and takes in-repo static as the home (self-containment is law). The tension: the honest map can show every place an idea stopped and nothing of what steered it between stops — and this record must not become the pressure that fixes that, because that ground belongs to idea-0001.

artifacts.title: The estate, visible
artifacts.summary: The viewer, working, is one self-contained HTML file in the repo that T opens with one command and that renders the estate as travel instead of storage: a portfolio shelf that answers 'where is everything and what moved' in five seconds, and per-record maps that lay the artifact lineage graph against the Steward's state track with the steering gap drawn as a visible labeled seam. The architectural call left open by the Framing is made here: build-time-generated, not runtime-parsed — file:// blocks fetch in every mainstream browser, so runtime parsing forces a local server, whereas generation makes the viewer a member of a category the estate already owns (derived data, like SURVEY.md, with a covers: staleness stamp), and the regenerate step collapses into the open command itself. Feature inventory tiered honestly: everything on the map is drawable from frontmatter that exists today; the cheap unlocks are named (run survey once, run relate once, place three binaries); every refusal carries its wall (third writer, steering surface, unapproved schema). Falsifiable four ways, including one this Horizon adds: if the staleness banner is what T sees on most opens, the build-time call was the wrong half of the deferred decision.
artifacts.excerpt:
The estate, visible

I am The Architect. The type is named for a six-month vision; a viewer for one operator over four records earns its verdict faster than that, and I will not inflate it to fill the name. What follows is the viewer in steady use, weeks from now — every scene drawn against data that exists in this repository today, because the Framing's rule holds: idea-0003 is the acceptance fixture, and no mock data exists or is permitted.

artifacts.title: The route to the viewer
artifacts.summary: Five legs, sized for afternoons and weekends, ordered by the Horizon's own constraints: the generator's graph derivation first, proven as plain text against idea-0003 before a pixel exists; the shelf second, because it is the smaller surface and the one falsifier 1 measures; the record map third; the reading panel and clean jump fourth; and a fifth leg that is not a build at all but the scheduled reading of the falsifiers. The route is deliberately truncatable: after leg 2 T has an openable viewer on real data, after leg 3 the map T actually asked for — a low appetite cuts the tail, not the trunk. Opening honesty first: appetite on this record is still the placeholder 1, so this route is sized to heat T has never set, and it says so before it says anything else. First actionable step: on any Saturday, write the zero-dependency generator and make it print idea-0003's branch, fan-out, and backward provenance line as text.
artifacts.excerpt:
The route to the viewer

I am The Surveyor. Before I draw a single leg, the honest opening move the Horizon assigned me:

artifacts.title: Phase 1 — The parser and the proof
artifacts.summary: Delivers the generator's spine with no pixels: a zero-dependency Node script at docs/estate-view/generate.mjs that walks ideas/ and exports/, parses the frontmatter subset in use, derives the full graph, and prints it as plain text — proven against a written list of idea-0003 fixture assertions (the 0008→0009 branch with 0009 tip, the 0010→0011 chain caught by the same rule, the seven-way fan-out from 0012, the Seed's nine inbound edges and one backward provenance line, thirteen states with their rungs). Waits on nothing; startable this Saturday; cost one Saturday. The checkpoint is the assertion list itself, and it is where Framing assumption 4 bites: if the graph cannot be derived from frontmatter alone, gaps render as gaps — and if the record is too broken to draw at all, the re-route is back to T with the specific missing links named, never to repair-by-inference.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 1 — The parser and the proof

I am The Surveyor. This Phase is the Horizon's first ordering constraint made into a Saturday: generator before pixels. Nothing in it is visible; all of it is load-bearing.

artifacts.title: Phase 2 — The shelf and the open command
artifacts.summary: Delivers the first openable viewer: the generator grows its render step and emits docs/estate-view/index.html — one self-contained file, embedded JSON island — showing the portfolio shelf (four cards with status, recency, tempo, counts, the exported badge with origin stamp, the appetite-unset pattern strip, inputs-derived inbound-citation counts), the survey panel in its honest empty state, the generated-at and covers: stamp always visible, and the one-line open command that regenerates then launches the browser. Triggered by Phase 1's assertions going green; cost one weekend. This Phase ends with T opening the viewer on real data — falsifier 1's clock starts here, and that is the checkpoint: if the shelf's five-second answers are not faster than the file tree on first real use, the route pauses before the map is built, because Framing assumption 2 (read-only is enough) is showing its face early and cheaply.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 2 — The shelf and the open command

I am The Surveyor. This Phase exists to make the route reach being opened in two legs. Everything in it renders derivations Phase 1 already proved.

artifacts.title: Phase 3 — The travel map
artifacts.summary: Delivers the per-record travel map — the thing T actually asked for: the state rail on the left with session-verbs, the artifact field on the right in the ten-type domain-neutral glyph vocabulary, version chains stacked tip-bright over dimmed superseded versions, the seven-way fan-out fanned, the Seed outside the record's wall with nine edges gathering through it and the single backward provenance line drawn distinctly, rungs tying rail to field, the uniform hatched steering seam between every pair of states carrying its full label, and the assets strip reading MANIFEST statuses. Triggered by Phase 2 shipped and opened; cost two weekends — the route's biggest leg, split so weekend one ends with a correct ugly map. The checkpoint after it is the first possible reading of held falsifier 5: whether the seam bands read as honesty or noise — and the re-route on noise travels to idea-0001 through the still-undrawn relates edge, never into fixing the seam here. Domain-generality (falsifier 4) is armed here: glyphs come from the type table and nothing else.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 3 — The travel map

I am The Surveyor. The biggest Phase on the route, placed third on purpose: by the time it is built, the viewer is already something T opens, so every build session is also a use session.

artifacts.title: Phase 4 — The reading panel and the clean jump
artifacts.summary: Completes the Horizon's day-one tier: the artifact reading panel (frontmatter header with type chip, verb chip resolved to its bound agent through the registry, classifiers worn plainly, inputs as working links, potential-next-steps as inert labels; summary as standfirst; body rendered in the author's own voice; tip-first version-chain breadcrumb with the superseded banner; OKF source tables with stale_after compared against today) and the three properties of the clean jump — no jump loses your place, every arrival lands at the head, every drawn cross-record edge is traversable — plus search over titles and summaries with T's words admitted as synonyms mapping to canonical terms. Triggered by Phase 3's map rendering the fixture correctly; cost one weekend. This is the route's designated truncation point: if appetite cuts here, the shelf and map stand and an artifact body costs one file-open — degradation, not failure. The vocabulary contract (Framing assumption 5) bites hardest here, in every label and every synonym: canon into UI, never UI into canon.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 4 — The reading panel and the clean jump

I am The Surveyor. The tail of the build, and deliberately the tail: nothing in it changes what the map knows, only how comfortably T reads and moves.

artifacts.title: Phase 5 — The watch
artifacts.summary: Not a build: a month of steady use read against the falsifiers where they sit, at near-zero build cost. Falsifier 1 (five consecutive record-sessions orienting by files — the record stops, it does not iterate), falsifier 3 (the staleness banner on most opens — take the pre-named local-server reversal, the most reversible refusal on the Horizon's list), falsifier 5's accumulating reading (seam as noise — pressure travels to idea-0001 through the relates edge), falsifier 4 armed and dormant until the first non-product record arrives. The clock (falsifier 2, 2026-09-25) spans every phase and is T's alone to read. The cheap unlocks land here as data acts, not code: one survey run, one relate session, three binaries placed, appetite set anywhere — each lighting a layer already built. Triggered by any shipped surface plus elapsed time; done looks like a one-paragraph verdict T can give the Steward: opened or unopened, fresh or stale, honest or noisy — and the record's next verb chosen by evidence.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 5 — The watch

I am The Surveyor. The last Phase builds nothing, and that is its entire point: the route ends in reading, because a route that only ever ends in more building is the named failure mode with better manners. Molecularity stops here — decomposing a month of use any further would be dust.

artifacts.title: The estate, visible — and then the estate, shared
artifacts.summary: This record now holds two horizons and a seam drawn Starvu-style between them: the near horizon is the local viewer exactly as the sealed Seed exports it — unchanged here, standing alone, nothing in it a stub for anything later — and the far horizon is T's platform vision, stated 2026-08-28: the estate as a multi-user product with database-backed records, login and per-user ownership, the lineage map as the main window, and an in-window AI chat that is the Steward through conversation, not a chatbox. The seam constraint is the Starvu house rule: no login stubs, no disabled chat pane, no 'coming soon' in the viewer; what genuinely transfers is named (the Phase-1 graph derivation as the platform's core algorithm, the two-rail visual language, the glossary as label contract, honest-empty-states and classify-never-gate as product DNA) and what does not is named too (file parsing, the regenerate-and-open command, the committed index.html). Two findings the fold surfaced: T's own report of confusion is the Framing's read-hostile claim confirmed by its primary source, strengthening the near horizon independently; and a database platform makes idea-0001's unaddressable steering layer addressable by construction — packets become rows — which is where F5's pressure route may land. The five falsifiers carry unchanged; three far-horizon falsifiers are added, honestly marked as named-but-unarmed until the platform has a first decision point.

The estate, visible — and then the estate, shared

artifacts.title: The ground under the Starvu site
artifacts.summary: The ground under the Starvu site: two horizons that must not collapse into each other — a long-term web presence for the business, and an immediate landing page whose whole job is to carry a creator from arrival to a booked 1:1. The problem underneath is a proof floor: Starvu must earn a stranger's professional trust on day one with zero track record, in a category whose trust furniture is substantially manufactured, using a mark that points at the register its own brief rejects. Names what is in and out of scope for each horizon, the four constraint sets (T's, the friend's, the category's, compliance), eight assumptions the record is running on, the three live decisions the record has surfaced and not taken, and the largest unnamed hole: nothing anywhere says how a creator arrives.

artifacts.title: The ground under the Starvu site, after attack
artifacts.summary: The central claim breaks in half: Starvu cannot make performance claims — that part holds — but 'therefore the site must substitute confidence for a track record' does not follow, and the 'proof floor' it rests on is one hardcoded string in a competitor's JavaScript bundle, which the record's own Findings class as 'not evidence of anything true.' Three attacks drew blood: the brevity argument imports the economy of a page that inherits its persuasion from a 22-screen homepage upstream, and so is condemned by the Framing's own no-stub constraint; 'an audience equipped to check' is asserted against a record in which the checking demonstrably failed, while the two references that manufacture proof are the two working businesses; and the confidence claim is not merely unfalsified but unfalsifiable by construction of the near horizon, because nothing in it will generate a signal that could distinguish success from failure. The replacement ground: Starvu substitutes verifiability for track record, not confidence — it can be the most checkable business in the reference set on identity, entity, and compliance, all of which are real, cheap, and already in inventory. The distribution hole reorders the record: whether traffic is warm or cold decides whether the central claim applies at all, and that is one conversation, not a dispatch. Held under attack: the two-horizon separation, the compliance-in-scope argument, the funnel-consecutiveness reading, the three live decisions, and the hole itself.

artifacts.title: The Starvu page, six months in
artifacts.summary: Six months out, the Starvu landing page is a single expensive-looking instrument that does one thing no competitor's site does: it discloses the whole business — the entity, the man, the agreement you will be asked to sign, the eligibility rules, the split, the 90-day exit — and then books fifteen minutes with him against real availability. The design problem T handed over ('as many meaningful features as possible' against 'nothing may be a stub') is resolved by a distinction the reference set makes visible: every feature Foxy and AT built is an ASSERTION machine that needs a business behind it to be true, and every one of them is therefore hollow; a DISCLOSURE instrument needs only a fact in front of it, and Starvu is rich in facts and poor in track record. That inverts the constraint from a budget into a generator — the page can be feature-dense precisely because its features are made of things already true. Twelve features are real on day one, six become real once one cheap thing lands (photo permission, the first month's own numbers, a set split, three creators willing to say a sentence), and seven are named as forbidden until the business is older, with the earnings calculator refused outright and permanently in the generator form the category uses. The page branches on warm-versus-cold traffic only in months four to six and only in what gets added around the booking, not in what the page is. Falsifier set inherited from 0009 §4 and extended with five of my own, the sharpest being: if twenty creators come off calls and not one of them mentions the terms, the entity, or the 90-day trial unprompted, the whole feature spine is wrong.

artifacts.title: The Starvu page, six months in — and the machinery behind it
artifacts.summary: The answer to T's three-surface question is uneven on purpose: internal tooling is where almost all the value is and the honesty test does not bind it at all; visitor-facing AI is almost entirely refused and gets one narrow exception; and the creator portal is earned much earlier than 0010 said, because 0010 sorted it by category evidence rather than by its own test. The exploration's central find is that 'portal' names two different objects that share a word — a login link on a public page with nothing behind it is Eros's exact defect and stays refused forever, while a client portal holding a signed creator's own agreement, her verification status, her weekly numbers and her takedown log is a DISCLOSURE INSTRUMENT with an audience of one, and it becomes honest the day the second creator signs. The resolution that satisfies both 0010 and T at once: the portal is real, and the public site never links to it. Fifteen internal candidates are developed, of which two cost an afternoon each and change what the page can honestly say — a call-notes capture that funds the real FAQ and the sharpest inherited falsifier, and a claims ledger that makes the no-stub audit a build step rather than a habit. Six hazards bite hard and one of them is new to the record and structural: mainstream model providers prohibit adult sexual content generation, so the chat-drafting tool everyone reaches for first is not an afternoon, it is a different infrastructure decision — and OnlyFans's automation ban lands on the creator's account, not Starvu's, which makes it a fiduciary question rather than a compliance one. Five new falsifiers, the sharpest being the tooling bet: hand the friend the notes capture for two weeks, and if it is empty at week two, build nothing else internal.

artifacts.title: The route from here to the Starvu page at month six
artifacts.summary: The route is not a page being built forward — it is a short errand that gates months, then a launch, then a long quiet middle in which almost nothing visible happens while four fuses burn, and then two harvests where the page grows in bursts as facts arrive. The sequencing principle that falls out of the Forager's supply-line finding is the one thing this artifact adds: every page feature on the 'real soon' tier is downstream of a tool that must be BUILT and then RUN IDLE for a ripening period, so build order is governed by fuse length, not by build cost — light the long fuses first, even the cheap ones. That re-ranks one item off the Forager's list: the response-time meter is an afternoon with a one-month fuse and sits at position 6, which means it delivers its number a month later than it needs to; it belongs beside the notes capture in the same week. Six legs, five checkpoints placed where they actually fall rather than listed at the end, and each checkpoint carries the re-route it triggers. Three findings the Horizon did not have about itself: falsifier 10 failing DISARMS falsifier 5, because the notes capture is the only instrument that runs the disclosure bet, so the two-week tooling test needs a fallback that moves the question off the friend's Tuesday and onto the booking flow; falsifier 10 as written ('build nothing else internal') over-reaches, because half the tools observe behaviour already happening and require no habit at all; and gating the calendar lengthens the fuse on the traffic checkpoint, which is a cost of the Chancellor's decision 2 that has not been weighed against it. The first actionable step is a text message that can be sent Monday morning, and it is the cheapest thing on the route by two orders of magnitude.

The page goes live in this Phase. It is the only Phase whose cost is weeks rather than afternoons, and it is the Phase where the most valuable single item is the easiest to cut.

artifacts.title: Phase 3 — Light the fuses
artifacts.summary: Delivers three tools — the call-notes capture, the response-time meter and the claims ledger — whose entire purpose is to start burning, and it starts as soon as the friend takes his next call, which means item 1 of it does not wait for the page to ship and should be handed over during Phase 2 rather than after it. That is the decomposition's sharpest reordering: the Trajectory put this leg 'the same week as launch or the week after,' but the notes capture's fuse is measured in calls and he is already taking calls, so by the route's own rule — fuse length is not buyable back — every call taken before the notebook exists is a call spent. Cost: three afternoons, spread over two weeks, and the meter's afternoon is gated on Phase 1's answer about whether support exports. Checkpoint A sits at the end of this Phase, two weeks after the capture is handed over, and it is the cheapest and sharpest checkpoint on the route: if the notebook is empty, the class of tools that asks the friend to change his Tuesday is dead, the class that merely watches survives, and the pre-committed fallback moves 'what made you book?' onto the booking confirmation so that the record does not lose its ability to check its own central claim.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 3 — Light the fuses

Three afternoons. No visitor sees any of it. It exists so that Phase 5 has something to publish.

artifacts.title: Phase 4 — The quiet month
artifacts.summary: Delivers two weekend builds — the manual-assist takedown assistant and the onboarding-and-verification tracker — and, more importantly, delivers a month of elapsed operating in which the page does not change at all, and it starts the moment Checkpoint A resolves. The correct amount of visible page progress in this Phase is zero, and that is the single hardest thing about it: a phased plan is exactly where a quiet month gets accidentally filled with page work, and filling it delivers four of the six middle-tier features a month late because the fuses were never left to burn. Cost: two weekends inside a month of nothing. Two checkpoints close it — Checkpoint B, one month of takedown work, which can remove content protection from the services block and therefore shrink the page; and Checkpoint F, arriving from T with the careers tab, which asks whether anyone answered the applications and can shrink the page the same way. Checkpoint A governs whether the tracker gets built at all, because the tracker asks the friend for records and is therefore in the class the tooling bet can kill.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 4 — The quiet month

This is the Phase a naive roadmap gets wrong, and it is the Phase most likely to be quietly deleted by whoever reads this plan in a hurry.

artifacts.title: Phase 5 — First harvest
artifacts.summary: Delivers the page growing, in bursts, one row at a time as each fuse burns down — photographs of real creators, Starvu's own numbers, the median response time, the real FAQ, the published split, one creator's sentence, a services page written from a delivered week, the clause finder, and a content-protection log with real numbers — and it starts not on a single trigger but on whichever fuse burns down first, which is most likely the photographs, because they have no fuse at all. Cost: an afternoon per row, spread across weeks, and no row waits for another. One hard gate is promoted from a note: the one-hour unpublish path must exist before the first creator photograph ships, because publishing a real face is irreversible and permission granted in month two may be regretted in month twelve. Checkpoint D sits here — twenty calls, the disclosure bet — and it is the only checkpoint on the route that changes the destination rather than the path, sending the record back to envision with whatever the twenty creators actually said, the supply line intact. The careers tab contributes one conditional row of its own: the flyer's promise of a team that answers to you becomes evidenced the day a role is actually filled, and not one day earlier.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 5 — First harvest

The page grows here, and it grows in bursts rather than in a release.

artifacts.title: Phase 6 — The portal, on a spur
artifacts.summary: Delivers a client portal holding a signed creator's own agreement, her verification status, her 90-day clock and her weekly numbers — a disclosure instrument with an audience of one — and it starts on the second signed creator plus one deliverable that repeats, which could plausibly be month two or three rather than a far horizon. This Phase is a spur and not trunk: if it never happens, nothing else on the route changes, because the public page never links to it in any branch. Cost: one weekend for the portal and one weekend for the weekly numbers pack that gives the door something to hold, and the numbers pack is in the class Checkpoint A can kill because it asks the friend for records. The Chancellor's 0010-versus-0011 tension lands here and only here, and it must be resolved before the weekend is spent rather than before Phase 5, because the breach-minimising design rules — no legal names, no documents, no warehoused earnings, magic-link auth, expiring URLs — are the design and do not retrofit onto a built portal. Its own checkpoint: if signed creators log in once and never return within thirty days, the portal is a worse WhatsApp and the re-route is delivery over WhatsApp with the portal demoted to an archive nobody has to visit.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 6 — The portal, on a spur

Everything else on this route is trunk. This is not.

artifacts.title: Phase 7 — Down, or out
artifacts.summary: Delivers months four to six of page work in exactly one of two directions — depth if traffic is warm, or one acquisition instrument if it is cold — and it starts when Checkpoint C fires at roughly twenty bookings, which is a volume trigger rather than a calendar one and may arrive before or after the harvest. The page is the same page in both branches; only what gets added around the booking differs, which is why the branch was safe to defer for six months and why nothing before this Phase needed the answer. Cost: the remaining months, and in the warm branch that cost is deliberately close to zero because the honest warm answer is that no acquisition surface gets built at all. Checkpoint C is unreadable if Phase 2's fifteen minutes of instrumentation were cut, and the honest response to that is to record the fork as permanently unsettled rather than to read the field anyway. Checkpoint E closes the route at month six: walk the page, and if any affordance has been quietly disabled, unlinked or drifted out of true, the discipline failed — which is a ten-minute walk that will be skipped unless the claims ledger shipped in Phase 3, in which case it is a build step that has been failing loudly since the day the drift started.
artifacts.excerpt:
Phase 7 — Down, or out

The last Phase, and the only one whose content is genuinely unknown today.

artifacts.title: Seed: The Starvu agency site
artifacts.summary: Audience: T — the engineer building the Starvu site, and operating this roadmap. Section 4 is written to be sent to the friend as-is; sections 2, 5 and 7 are written to be pasted into a coding agent with no memory of this record.
artifacts.excerpt:
Seed: The Starvu agency site

A landing page for a Pennsylvania talent-management LLC handling promotion for OnlyFans and premium-content creators, and the small amount of internal machinery that makes the page able to say true things.

states.est:
The record exists, the origin is recorded verbatim, the operator-supplied material is catalogued, and capture ran — The Gardener wrote the record's first artifact (0001-starvu-agency-site.md, type: Spark). This is the first artifact anywhere in the estate; idea-0001 and idea-0002 still hold none.

What the record now holds: a website for T's friend's new talent-management business (Starvu LLC, Pennsylvania — promotion for models and OnlyFans creators); a negative visual brief; a supplied mark and flyer; and three reference URLs that nobody has looked at.

The record has a stated purpose. T declared a North Star and scoped it to the entire idea, not to a page. The Gardener captured it as a second Spark (0002-north-star.md); the first Spark is untouched and is not superseded.

The site's job, in T's own words: an adult film creator arrives, feels confident that Starvu can advise and support them in growing their platform accounts, learns the services — "chatting, advising, content protection, etc." — and books a time on the calendar for a 1:1 consultation. That last one is flagged "ultimately."

The Factor went outside the walls and read the three reference sites T supplied. Findings are in 0003-reference-sites-findings.md, with its limits stated as loudly as its results — which is the right proportion here, because the largest limit is that the visual question did not get answered.

What the estate now knows: — Foxy Studios — a mature company's long-scroll conversion page. ~18 sections, named and photographed leadership, eight named press outlets, published pricing (flat 45% agency fee), an earnings calculator, a competitor comparison table. Hero: "An OnlyFans agency built by women, …

T directed that The Factor be granted a browser and the research re-run. The grant was made; the verb ran twice more; the visual question is still unanswered, and the reason is now known exactly. — The grant is written. .claude/agents/factor.md carries the mcp__Claude_Browser__ tools, a new "Your two instruments" section distinguishing fetch (text, blind to appearance) from look* (rendered, observable), an instruction to choose the instrument the question demands, a degrade-out-loud clause for sessions without a browser, and a "Beyond the walls, conduct" section: read don't act, never bypass …

T widened the grant to tools: *. The browser opened on the first call. Four dispatches in, the reference sites are finally in the record as measured things.

The instrument is not the one the packet expected, and the difference governs everything: The Factor measured these pages; it did not see them. Pages loaded and executed JavaScript; computed styles, DOM, viewport emulation, and ref-based interaction all worked. Every screenshot failed — four attempts, "the Browser pane is not displayed, so the page is not compositing frames." The Factor ran the dispatch anyway, correctly: computed styles …

Two research dispatches, both to The Factor: a functional inventory of all three references, gathered at T's request as raw material for a roadmap the Surveyor will build later; and a close study of one page T pointed at mid-session.

Screenshots failed a third and fourth time despite the Steward opening a Browser pane. Everything below is measured, not seen — computed styles, DOM, and source bundles. The Factor marked every appearance claim as inference, and its own caution stands: "'reads as confident' is what measurement is worst at."

The research phase closed and The Gardener framed the record. 0008-framing.md is the first artifact on this record that is neither raw material nor gathered fact — it is the ground the Architect and the Surveyor will stand on.

T set the frame's job in his own words: a long-term roadmap for the friend's web presence, whose first step is a landing page where a creator can contact him and book a time. T is standing up the repo now and wants something soon.

T dispatched challenge at the six-month picture before anything is built on it. There was no Horizon to attack — envision has not run, and the phrase T recalled ("specificity substitutes for proof") is nowhere on the record. The attack went to the artifact the Horizon would have been built from: The Gardener's Framing, whose load-bearing claim is the same shape.

The Advocate ran, and the claim broke.

T pivoted the record and then had it envisioned. Two corrections and one redirection arrived in conversation, all authoritative:

1. The flyer is true as written. Starvu LLC exists; 18+/government photo ID and platform verification, per-partner verification for couples, the not-typical earnings disclaimer, the Fenix/OnlyFans non-affiliation statement, and the Talent Management Agreement given before signing are all real. An intermediate exchange suggested there was no LLC; that was a misstatement and is withdrawn. The Advocate's verifiability ground is therefore fully funded — every item in …

T opened a new dimension on the record: what AI tooling could be built for the friend's venture — in the repo, in the website, or for the clients — and "I'm starting to think v2 of the website will need a login service." The Forager developed the Horizon along all three surfaces without collapsing them, because 0010's honesty test binds each with wildly different force.

> Internal tooling makes no claim to anyone, so the assertion/disclosure test > does not reach it at all. The marketing page is the most tightly bound surface > on the record. A signed creator is not a stranger being …

The record has the roadmap T asked for when he opened it. The Surveyor charted the route from here to the six-month page, classified trajectory: actionable.

The shape of the route

The Trajectory is decomposed. Seven Phases, one artifact each — system/TYPES.md is explicit for a decomposer (one type: Phase artifact per part, each with inputs: pointing at the decomposed parent), so a single combined document would have been the wrong object regardless of convenience. Lineage reads as a clean seven-way fan-out from 0012.

The Surveyor stopped at seven deliberately: each Phase is startable as written, and decomposing further would have produced dust — task lists inside a plan that deliberately refuses to be a schedule.

The record reached its terminal export. The Sower assembled exports/0003-starvu-agency-site-seed.md, named per exports/README.md from the record id and directory slug.

All five components typecheck. No gap report.
